summary: Build adaptive MEAL data workflows, dashboards, and feedback loops for accountable programme decisions. Explore the practical course.
lede: Data-driven adaptive MEAL systems connect monitoring evidence and community feedback to programme decisions. This course is for intermediate MEAL and programme practitioners who need to make evidence usable in operational decisions. Learners practise mapping data flows, checking data quality, designing dashboard requirements, and converting community feedback into documented adaptations to targeting, delivery, or resource allocation.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who connect programme evidence, community accountability, and operational decisions across humanitarian, development, and social protection settings. It suits intermediate practitioners who already work with monitoring data and need a more disciplined approach to adaptive MEAL systems.
prerequisites: You should have practical experience with programme monitoring, evaluation, accountability, learning, or results-based management. Familiarity with indicators, logical frameworks, Theory of Change, partner reporting, or community feedback is recommended. No coding or programming is required. Advanced methods such as outcome harvesting, Most Significant Change, contribution analysis, AI-assisted data cleaning, and dashboard automation receive conceptual and operational treatment rather than production engineering depth. Bring a laptop if possible for digital template exercises.
